rationale: A unanimous affirmance will likely be written narrowly around Singleton and Hormel, emphasizing that considering newly raised appellate theories is a prudential, fairness-based discretion and that the Tenth Circuit’s “certainty/beyond reasonable doubt” safety valve is permissible. Roberts is most likely to keep the opinion institutional and restrained, though Kagan is a strong alternative to craft an administrable, incentives-focused articulation of forfeiture discretion.
